title: Graceful GPU eviction workflows with priority-aware fallback and autoscaler handshake
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Upgrades to Dedicated GPU pools currently rely on blunt node drains that cause sudden capacity drops and elevated tail latency for customer traffic. We need a structured, version-safe eviction workflow that coordinates with the cluster autoscaler and router to ensure capacity-safe rollouts across LTS channels. Goal: implement a handshake protocol and priority-aware eviction phases (soft->hard) with preflight capacity snapshots, slow-drain windows, and automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants when SLOs degrade. This ticket delivers the orchestration layer, runtime hooks for drains, and operator playbooks for emergency rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled drain API that marks a GPU node with drain-phase metadata (preflight, soft, hard, completed)
Autoscaler handshake: drain agent requests autoscaler reservation and receives an explicit guarantee window or is throttled
Router integration: traffic weights adjusted incrementally during soft-drain and canary phases
SLO guards: automatic pause and rollback of drain if p50/p95 latency or error-rate thresholds are violated for > 3m
Observability events emitted for each drain-phase transition and a consolidated rollout timeline in Console
Automated e2e test that simulates 20% of fleet drains and validates no more than 5% SLO regressions for a 10-minute sustained period
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with infra, serving-runtime, and autoscaler owners. Agreed on soft vs hard eviction definitions and minimal signal set (NODE_DRAIN_PHASE, DRAIN_TARGET_CAPACITY, DRAIN_VERSION).

2026-03-03: Spike completed: implemented drain-agent prototype that emits preflight capacity snapshot and requests a 'reservation token' from autoscaler mock. Found race when multiple drains target same GPU pool—will add pool-level serialisation.

2026-03-05: Design review with PM and Console team. Decided to use existing rollout timeline UI to display drain phases and to add new events for 'autoscaler reservation granted/denied'. Minor API modification requested: include expected eviction window length in seconds.

2026-03-08: PR opened for drain-controller core: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821. Includes state machine and webhook for router weight adjustments. Running unit tests in CI; integration still blocked by autoscaler API changes.

2026-03-10: Canary plan drafted. Wave sizes and inter-wave pauses defined. Added temporary fallback policy to redirect traffic to quantized model variants when pool capacity < 90% and SLOs are at risk.
decisions: Use a 3-phase drain state machine: PREVIEW (preflight snapshot), SOFT_DRAIN (gradual traffic shift + pod eviction with graceful termination), HARD_DRAIN (force eviction after window)
Autoscaler must provide explicit reservation tokens with TTL; if no token then drain pauses for backoff windows to prevent cascading capacity loss
Router will implement linear weight ramp-down over soft-drain window; default soft-drain window = 600s configurable per-release
Fallbacks favored over aggressive evacuation: prefer routing to compatible model variants or cross-region routing before hard evicting customer-serving pods
Expose drain events and progress to Console with rollout-level SLO overlays to enable human-in-the-loop aborts
test_plan: Unit tests for drain state transitions and TTL expiration handling
Integration test using k8s-kind cluster + autoscaler stub that simulates reservation grants/denials
Load test in staging with 30% of a 100-node pool drained in waves; run benchmark traffic and validate SLO thresholds
Chaos test: deny autoscaler reservation mid-drain to validate safe pause behavior and rollback triggers
runbook_and_playbook: Operator checklist for manual abort: steps to pause drains, reassign traffic, and rehydrate capacity from reserved pools
Emergency rollback: route weight restoration script, and steps to revert runtime flags and model pins
Postmortem templates and required telemetry snapshots to collect when an SLO breach occurs during rollout
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Multiple concurrent drains on the same pool could starve capacity. Mitigation: pool-level serialisation and autoscaler reservation tokens.
Risk: Router weight changes may cause short-lived cache misses and thundering KV cache pressure. Mitigation: introduce small ramp steps and cache-warming prefetch during soft-drain.
Risk: Fallback policies may change quality of responses. Mitigation: label fallbacks in Console and only enable automatic fallback when quality loss is audited and within acceptable bounds.
